question: With the production Runtime unchanged since the Discovery measurement, do the five blind Holdout games stop inside the same shared public contracts Discovery already exposed, or do they require behavior that can only be expressed per game?
current_uncertainty: Discovery showed that eight of ten games stop inside already implemented public contracts, but Discovery samples could have been unrepresentative of their clusters.
Three Holdout clusters (Qt, SDL, SoupeAuCaillou) were never exercised dynamically, so it is unknown whether they introduce contract families outside the Discovery set.

expected_outcome_a.result: Holdout games stop inside contract families Discovery already exposed, at a reuse ratio of at least 0.70, with no requirement expressible only through game identity.
excludes: the explanation that the Discovery convergence was an artifact of the Discovery sample choice

expected_outcome_b.result: Holdout games stop mostly on families absent from Discovery, or at least one needs game-specific state, identity or return values.
excludes: the explanation that the public compatibility layer generalizes beyond the games used to find it

why_cheaper_test_is_insufficient: A blind holdout is only meaningful when executed against the compiled Runtime; static analysis cannot show which contract a game reaches first, and no production change has been made that a cheaper focused contract could re-verify.
notes: No production Runtime change was made between Discovery and Holdout, so the holdout measures generalization of the existing public layer rather than of a fix round. Discovery evidence is run 35654415068.
